newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fokker says survival hinges on Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Fokker says survival hinges on Malaysia.

text.p: Bankrupt Dutch aircraft maker Fokker NV said on Thursday Dutch parties involved in talks on a last-minute deal to relaunch the company had reached agreement and that its fate now hinged on obtaining the support of Malaysian company Khazanah Nasional.

A statement released by the court-appointed administrators who have been running Fokker since it was declared bankrupt a year ago said the Dutch parties had reached agreement on the text of a memorandum of understanding for a relaunch of Fokker.
The statement identified the parties to the agreement as the Dutch state, engineering group Stork, Deleye Investment Group and the administrators.
It said these parties would now start negotiations with Khazanah Nasional of Malaysia to obtain its involvement in the relaunch plan and the memorandum of understanding.

The memorandum of understanding envisages that the Dutch state, Malaysian government-owned Khazanah, Stork and Deleye Investment will set up a new company which will acquire the aircraft-making assets of the bankrupt Fokker.
The statement said all parties were aiming to complete the relaunch plan by May 1, adding that it was of "essential importance" that everybody involved could agree on a solid business plan.
It said the Fokker administrators had repeated that holders of Fokker shares would not receive any payment even if the relaunch could be successfully completed.
